candidates.name: Look-Ahead-Bench - runnable standard that turns the leakage audit into a measured number
candidates.improves_agent: WOLF (signal/backtest leakage gate) first, then Hartley Capital model-build promotion and Prism alt-data timestamping
candidates.what: arXiv 2601.13770 (open code github.com/benstaf/lookaheadbench). Standardized benchmark of look-ahead bias in point-in-time finance LLMs: quantifies leakage as alpha decay across temporally distinct market regimes vs quantitative baselines, separating genuine prediction from memorization. Standard LLMs leak; point-in-time Pitinf models generalize and improve with scale.
candidates.why: Tool form of the 06-19 Profit-Mirage leakage-audit lesson and the 06-20 live-eval gate. Converts the manual leakage checklist into a measured, repeatable score with published baselines, plus a model-selection rule: prefer point-in-time-trained models; reject any signal whose edge decays across regime splits (the tell-tale of leaked future info). Sharpens an existing agent, adds zero headcount. Pragma resale: standardized look-ahead-bias benchmark on a client model before capital is risked.
candidates.action: Logged as today's lesson + folded into WOLF leakage-audit gate as the RUNNABLE standard (measure look-ahead bias as alpha decay across regime splits; prefer point-in-time-trained models). No live code changed. Wiring into live WOLF promotion code = NEEDS BOBBY APPROVAL.

candidates.name: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 - security checklist + memory-poisoning guard for the shared corpus
candidates.improves_agent: Sentinel (security posture) + whole-fleet memory architecture (shared corpus /Atlas/harvard-library, wolf_live_data.json, self-improving-loop agent-lessons.md)
candidates.what: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (2026): goal hijacking, tool misuse, identity abuse, memory poisoning, etc. Companion: Microsoft Agent Governance Toolkit (open-source runtime security).
candidates.why: The fleet's most distinctive asset - one agent's learnings shared with every other agent via file memory - is also its biggest memory-poisoning surface: a bad write to the shared corpus or agent-lessons.md propagates fleet-wide. OWASP names this a top risk; fix is a provenance/validation step on shared-memory writes (dovetails with Managed-Agents Memory audit trails already logged). Additive, defensive, zero edge-risk.
candidates.action: Logged as fleet security checklist; memory poisoning flagged as priority guard for shared corpus + self-improving-loop (validate provenance on shared-memory writes before they propagate). Building an actual write-validation gate = NEEDS BOBBY APPROVAL (touches live memory).

candidates.name: Governed per-agent identity + attributable audit (Autopilots / Entra / Agent Governance Toolkit)
candidates.improves_agent: Fleet architecture (attributable per-agent actions, pairs with audit-trail goal) + Pragma resale (agent-governance audit)
candidates.what: Microsoft Autopilots pattern - each agent under its own governed identity (not a shared service account) so every action is attributable; runtime enforcement + auditing + lineage/provenance.
candidates.why: Attribution/audit half is good discipline and resaleable. BUT the always-on half cuts against the lean-fleet/scheduled-fire discipline - always-on agents burn continuously and fail their own CBS. Adopt identity+audit; reject always-on unless a specific agent clears its breakeven.
candidates.action: Note attributable per-agent identity/audit as a target discipline (consistent with RULE ZERO single-Chrome + existing file-memory layout); explicitly do NOT move the fleet to always-on. Per-agent governed-identity infra = NEEDS BOBBY APPROVAL.
